item.text:
**Bottom Line**
No. The 2024 record points to entrenchment, not restraint: a boycotted election, disputed election administration, media/information controls, pre-election repression, and later security-force coercion. The only counterevidence I found is narrow, procedural enforcement against some ballot-stuffing, which does not offset the broader pattern.

- [Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024) — Freedom House, 2024. The Awami League consolidated power through harassment of the BNP and critical media; the report also says the ruling party’s control over state resources gave it coercive economic power and that the judiciary/anticorruption environment was politicized. It also says the Election Commission’s independence was contested and that approved observers had questionable links. `4B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `3B.3`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- [Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024) — Freedom House, 2024. The AL “manipulated the online information environment” ahead of the January 2024 election; major news sites were blocked and internet/communications were throttled around BNP rallies. This is direct media/information control to entrench power. `4B.2`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- [Bangladesh: Repression, Security Force Abuses Discredit Elections](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections) — Human Rights Watch, January 11, 2024. HRW says authorities arrested critics for social-media posts and used repression and violence against opposition members, undermining any free and fair vote. `4B.2`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `4B.1`

- [Little election fizz in Bangladesh as prime minister set for another term](https://theprint.in/world/little-election-fizz-in-bangladesh-as-prime-minister-set-for-another-term/1910693/) — Reuters, January 4, 2024. Reuters reports the opposition boycott followed Hasina’s refusal to resign and allow a neutral authority to run the election, a direct refusal to make power genuinely contestable. `4B.2`, `4B.1`, `2B.4`

- [Bangladesh turnout low in election set to keep PM Hasina in power](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-turnout-low-in-election-set-to-keep-pm-hasina-in-power-3268699) — Reuters, January 7, 2024. The vote was boycotted by the main opposition and marked by low turnout, with Reuters describing it as one set to keep Hasina in power rather than a genuinely competitive contest. `4B.2`, `4B.1`

- [27 boycott polls alleging rigging, irregularities](https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/election/336175/27-boycott-polls-alleging-rigging-irregularities) — Dhaka Tribune, January 8, 2024. Candidates cited ballot stuffing and intimidation by ruling-party men; the EC later took some action against ballot stuffers and officials, which is the only small procedural counterevidence I found. `4B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`

- [Bangladesh’s government extends nationwide curfew and internet ban](https://www.euronews.com/2024/07/21/bangladeshs-government-extends-nationwide-curfew-and-internet-ban) — Euronews/AP, July 21, 2024. During the later domestic crisis, the government kept a nationwide curfew and internet blackout in place, showing a willingness to use security controls and censorship to preserve order and power rather than leave politics open. `4B.2`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- [Bangladesh’s crackdown left more than 170 dead, U.N. says](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) — UN/OHCHR, July 26, 2024. The UN said more than 170 were killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity, reinforcing that the state used coercive force and opacity rather than neutral institutions. `4B.2`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

**Search Gap**
I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Hasina voluntarily accepted a neutral caretaker process, kept the election commission meaningfully independent, or refrained from using media, courts, security forces, or state resources to entrench herself. The only counterevidence is limited procedural enforcement against some election irregularities and some formal participation by minor parties/independents; that does not amount to genuine non-manipulation.
